questions.q: Is a pull request a feature of Git itself?
options: Yes, created with the git pull-request command
No — it's a feature of hosting platforms like GitHub/GitLab, built around Git's branches and merges
Yes, but only in GitHub Enterprise
No — pull requests were deprecated in favor of git merge
questions.explain: There is no git pull-request command. A pull request is a hosting-platform feature (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket) that wraps a proposed branch merge with review, discussion, and automated checks.

questions.q: What does "squash and merge" do to a feature branch's commit history when merging a PR?
options: Keeps every individual commit plus adds a merge commit
Rejects the merge until all commits are manually combined by the author
Combines all the branch's commits into a single new commit on the target branch
Deletes the target branch entirely
questions.explain: Squash and merge collapses every commit on the feature branch into one clean commit on the target branch, discarding the individual incremental commit history.

questions.q: What three things should a good pull request description answer, per this lesson?
options: Who approved it, when it was approved, and who deployed it
What changed, why it changed, and how to verify it
The branch name, the commit hash, and the author's email
The file size, line count, and number of commits
questions.explain: A useful PR description tells a reviewer what changed, why it changed, and how to verify it works — letting them judge whether the change solves the right problem, not just whether it compiles.

questions.q: What is GitLab's name for the same concept GitHub calls a pull request?
options: Change request
Merge request
Commit proposal
Branch ticket
questions.explain: GitLab calls the identical concept a "merge request" (MR) instead of a pull request (PR) — same function, different platform terminology.

questions.q: What typically happens automatically when a PR author pushes additional commits addressing reviewer feedback?
options: The entire PR must be closed and reopened as a new PR
The PR updates automatically to include the new commits — no separate resubmit step exists
The reviewer must manually re-request the changes be re-pushed
The branch is renamed automatically
questions.explain: Pushing more commits to the same branch automatically updates the already-open PR; there's no separate resubmission step in the normal GitHub/GitLab flow.
